placements: Both establish programming foundations, including structured and object-oriented programming, testing and debugging.
Both teach algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis.
Both cover relational databases, SQL, data modelling and normalization.
Both develop software through requirements, design, testing, maintenance and quality assurance.
Both provide formal logic and discrete structures for computational reasoning; the UCR course integrates these with algorithm construction.
Operating systems and networks develop related computer-systems foundations. Leiden distributes its systems requirements across two courses.
Both introduce differentiation, integration and mathematical methods used in computing and data science.
Both extend calculus to multivariable and more advanced analytical methods.
Both introduce matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations.
Both establish probability distributions, estimation and probabilistic reasoning for computer science.
Both apply multivariate statistical modelling, regression and experimental analysis to data.
Both teach regression, classification, clustering and evaluation of predictive models.
Both develop neural-network models and apply them to complex data.
Search methods overlap. UCR extends them into numerical and adversarial optimization, while Leiden covers additional forms of symbolic reasoning.
Both study agents that learn behaviour through reinforcement.
Perception and action provide background on human cognition. Leiden applies this area to the design of conversational agents.
Cognitive neuroscience contributes evidence on attention and memory. Leiden also examines computational models of cognition.
Both examine fairness, responsibility, privacy and ethical questions raised by artificial intelligence.
Both develop research design, operationalisation, experiments, sampling and statistical inference.
Both introduce human cognition and its neural basis; Leiden connects this foundation explicitly to computation.
Both cultivate academic development, presentation and reflection on study progression.
